mission: Let an ops-write apply match its dry run: the remaining-50 approved list hashed replan_observed_at (the re-plan's database now()), so every re-plan produced a new SHA-256 and the apply refused even for an unchanged list (run 38972369303, nothing written). The list now holds content only (batch, count, resolver version, entries); a moved digest or changed sibling set still changes the SHA and refuses the apply. Staging only; no collector, setting, price, identity, Market Value/Index, secret or Railway change; no deploy, enqueue or runbook run in this PR.

impacts.reason: approved_list() drops replan_observed_at from the hashed document (replan.json still records observed_at). The #116 tool never read that field. Entries, guards, eligibility, count and the apply's expected_sha256 check are unchanged.
Asserts two re-plans that differ only in time hash the same, and a moved digest changes the SHA.

resources.name: GitHub Actions: ops-write enqueue-remaining-50 approved-list SHA (scripts/ops/replan.py)

impact.deployment_impact: Ops tooling and test only. collector_services is empty and no raw_dependency_migration: 0 collector rollouts, no DDL. No path under services/, packages/, apps/ or .github/ changes.

recovery.procedure: Native revert of this PR restores the timestamped list (applies then refuse again). No data, schema, provider or service configuration to undo.
recovery.trigger: An apply that passes its SHA check while a candidate's digest or sibling set differs from the dry run's list.
recovery.backup: Not applicable: no schema or row change. Railway Postgres daily backups continue.

verification.observation_window: After merge: a new remaining-50 dry run and its apply (both owner-approved) report the same approved_list_sha256, and the apply writes 50 intents.
